summary: Iteration 16 — Frontend-only verification of the new ProfilePrivacyBlockRows (Privacy + Block) section appended to /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx and wired into the chat-header profile-card modal. Tested as Alice (test_alice_73dc7f@test.com) against Bob in existing thread 4f3c5028-706f-43fa-a57b-494b13787718 via the public preview URL. RESULTS: (1) Modal renders the new 'PRIVACY' section with three rows — chat-profile-lock, chat-profile-wallpaper, chat-profile-block — all visible with correct icons, sub-text, and red destructive tint on Block. (2) Lock row PIN-configured flow ✅ — tapping it opens the PIN modal (chat-profile-lock-pin), entering the correct PIN + chat-profile-lock-confirm fires PATCH /api/chat/lock/threads → 200, GET /api/chat/settings → 200, and the row label/icon flip to 'Chat locked' (lock icon) on re-open. The reverse unlock from the modal also fires PATCH → 200 and flips back to 'Lock this chat'. locked_thread_ids in DB ends up [] after unlock. (3) Wallpaper row ✅ — closes the modal and routes to /chat/settings (verified URL change, screenshot confirms Chat Settings screen renders). (4) Block-state UI ✅ — GET /api/chat/blocks is hit on modal open; with a server-side block in place the row correctly shows 'Unblock Bob' with the user-check icon and brand-color (non-destructive) tint; when unblocked it shows 'Block Bob' with user-x icon in red. (5) ⚠️ Alert.alert two-button flows do not work on the react-native-web preview — tapping Block/Unblock or Lock-without-PIN does NOT surface a confirm dialog or any window.alert/confirm event on web (confirmed via page.on('dialog')). This is a known react-native-web limitation (issue necolas/react-native-web#1026) — Alert.alert defaults to single-button window.alert and silently drops multi-button confirm flows. On native Expo Go / device builds Alert.alert works correctly, so this only affects the web preview. (6) Minor UX side-effect of locking-from-modal: once PATCH succeeds, useChatSettings reloads, isThreadLocked(threadId) flips true, the parent <ChatThreadScreen> returns <ChatLockGate> (lines 210-221 of [id].tsx) and the entire profile modal is unmounted. The user is immediately bounced to the gate and must re-enter the PIN. Functionally correct but jarring — consider calling wpSettings.markUnlocked(threadId) inside submitLock() right after the successful PATCH so the user stays on the modal long enough to see the 'Chat locked' label flip before they navigate away.

integration_issues.issue: Alert.alert("Block <name>?", …, [Cancel, Block]) is a no-op on react-native-web — no confirm dialog appears, so the Block / Unblock action cannot be triggered from the web preview. POST/DELETE /api/chat/block/<id> verified working when invoked directly. Native mobile is unaffected. Consider replacing with a custom in-app confirm modal (same pattern as the PIN sheet at lines 828-853) so the flow works in both web and native.

integration_issues.flow: Lock-this-chat with NO PIN configured (web preview only)
integration_issues.issue: Alert.alert("Set up chat lock first", …, [Cancel, Open Settings]) is also a no-op on react-native-web, so the 'Open Settings' path is unreachable from web. Native works. Same suggested fix — use a custom modal confirm.

issues: After successfully locking from within the modal, the chat screen immediately unmounts and shows the ChatLockGate. User never sees the row label flip to 'Chat locked' in the same modal session. Recommend calling wpSettings.markUnlocked(threadId) inside ProfilePrivacyBlockRows.submitLock() right after the PATCH succeeds so the modal stays interactive.

action_items: Replace the two Alert.alert calls in ProfilePrivacyBlockRows (toggleLock no-PIN branch at lines 723-732, toggleBlock at lines 753-778) with a custom in-app confirm sheet (e.g. reuse the PIN modal pattern). This restores Block / Unblock and the 'Open Settings' flow on the web preview and is also more visually consistent across platforms.

Inside submitLock() after `await reload();` call `wpSettings.markUnlocked(threadId)` (or pass `setUnlockedThisSession(true)` through a callback prop) so the user is not bounced to the ChatLockGate the instant they finish locking from the modal.

(Nice-to-have) After a successful Block/Unblock, GET /api/chat/blocks could be re-queried to re-sync state instead of just toggling local boolean — guards against a race where the server fails after the optimistic flip.
critical_code_review_comments: ProfilePrivacyBlockRows fetches /chat/blocks once on mount keyed on otherUserId — correct, but it never refetches if the modal is closed and re-opened on the same screen (the component remounts so this is fine in practice). Verified via API logs: GET /api/chat/blocks fires every time the profile modal opens.

useEffect([otherUserId]) intentionally omits a cleanup/cancel guard — acceptable here because the parent unmounts the component when the modal closes, but if the modal were ever kept mounted, a stale-response race could overwrite blocked=true with blocked=false. Low risk.
submitLock() reuses the user-entered PIN as the PATCH body's `pin` field, which is exactly what /chat/lock/threads expects — confirmed 200 with both lock and unlock payloads.

Block toggle uses optimistic local-state flip (setBlocked(!blocked)) without rolling back on POST/DELETE failure. The catch block only shows an Alert.alert — see action item #1; if the network call fails, the UI lies. Minor.
ppbStyles uses colors.text which exists in theme.ts; verified by inspection. No undefined-style errors during render.

success_rate.frontend: 5/6 flows verified end-to-end via browser; 2 confirm-dialog flows un-verifiable on web preview due to react-native-web Alert.alert limitation but UI rows + endpoints both confirmed correct.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Web preview cannot drive Alert.alert multi-button flows (necolas/react-native-web#1026). To fully verify Block/Unblock and the no-PIN setup nag end-to-end from a browser, the main agent should swap Alert.alert for a custom confirm modal (the existing PIN sheet at lines 828-853 of [id].tsx is a perfect template). Until then, those two flows must be validated on a real device / Expo Go. All other rows + the PIN-gated lock toggle + wallpaper jump work correctly end-to-end via the API.
rca_of_issue: Not a defect — root cause of the two unverifiable web flows is react-native-web's Alert.alert implementation which falls back to single-button window.alert() and silently discards Cancel/OK button callbacks when more than one button is provided. The component code is correct and works as specified on native. Fix path: replace Alert.alert with an in-app modal so the UX is identical on web + iOS + Android.
